title: Hybrid routing & model selection sprint — catalog walkthrough
summary: Demo-focused walkthrough of Redwood's model catalog filters, benchmark interpretation, and hybrid routing playbook. Key ask: help LumenHealth pick 2 open models for a pilot that balance latency and accuracy for clinical summarization, and validate fallback routing for burst traffic. Security and data residency concerns discussed; agreed to share benchmark spreadsheet and security pack.
topics: security: KMS, audit logs, SOC2, data residency
next steps: pilot shortlist + benchmarking run
transcript: 00:00 Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Um, quick round of intros? 00:07 Alex (LumenHealth CTO): Alex here, CTO at LumenHealth. We're evaluating inference options for a clinical note summarization pipeline. 00:12 Jordan: Awesome. Priya and Mateo from the engineering side will run the demo, and we'll show the catalog + routing playbook. 00:18 Rina (ML Platform): Hi, Rina — ML platform lead. Our main constraints: sub-300ms p50 on short notes, cost under $0.0008/token target, and strict PHI handling — so VPC or private is likely. 00:30 Samir (Security): Samir, security. Need SOC 2 + audit logs and customer KMS. 00:36 Jordan: Got it. We'll point out the Private deployment options and the security docs link at the end. 00:40 Jordan: Ok Priya, kick us off with the catalog. 00:43 Priya (Redwood SE): Sure. I'm opening the model catalog — top left you see filters. We can filter by task, e.g., summarization, and then by latency profile, quantization, and hardware compatibility. Notice the 'benchmarks' column: we surface p50/p95 latency from our hosted runs plus a cost per token estimate. The trick — and this is important — is to read the bench notes. 01:10 Priya: For clinical text, we often pick a 7B-ish open model quantized to int8 on A10G or similar; it gives a reasonable quality/cost tradeoff. See example: model 'borealis-7b-clin' — listed as 240ms p50 on short sequences, but p95 climbs with long context. 01:27 Jules (PM): Are those numbers coming from your internal hosted infra or customer-shaped runs? 01:31 Priya: Mixed. The catalog shows our standard hosted benchmarks (default prompt mix) and then 'sampled' customer-replay numbers when available. There's a link to the raw sheet for each model — e.g., "benchmarks/lumenhealth-sample-2026-05.xlsx" for pilot runs we'll produce. 01:45 Mateo (Redwood): One caveat: transcription in the catalog can mis-say some kernel mappings; we surface favored kernels per device, but actual kernel selection is dynamic at runtime. 01:56 Rina: Quick Q: how do you handle fallback when the chosen model is under heavy load? We can't have our UX fall back to an obviously lower-quality model. 02:05 Priya: Good question. We demo routing policies: you can set policy precedence — strict quality first, then latency SLO, then cost. For LumenHealth we might pick: prefer model A for quality, if capacity breaches 90% then route to model B with similar evaluation delta < 1.5 ROUGE points, otherwise use small-run queueing or degrade non-critical routes. We also support automatic A/B routing so you can parallel-run both and compare. 02:34 Alex: What's the mechanism for model version pinning? We need stable outputs for audits. 02:39 Priya: You pin a model revision in your deployment config. The console shows model hashes and rollout options — canary, gradual traffic shift, or cold fallback. 02:48 Samir: And for PHI: can logs be disabled or masked? 02:51 Jordan: Yes — in Private you control logs and retention. In Hosted we offer redaction and token-level retention controls; we'll share the security pack. 02:58 Jordan: Okay we're going to walk through a concrete selection. Demo time. 03:02 Priya: I'm applying filters: task=summarization, data-domain=clinical, max-p95-latency=600ms, max-cost-per-token=$0.001, hardware=A100 or A10G. The result set shows 5 models. 03:18 Priya: I'm selecting 3 candidates: 'open-clarity-7B-v2', 'borealis-7b-clin' and 'medlite-13B-q4'. Note medlite 13B has better ROUGE in our evals but costs ~2x tokens; it also benefits more from A100 kernel mapping. 03:35 Jules: What's medlite's quantization? q4? 03:38 Mateo: It's q4_0 in the catalog, which we've validated for latency vs accuracy; for clinical you might try q4 with a short calibration set. 03:45 Rina: Are your benchmark numbers reproducible on our infra if we run the same model? 03:49 Priya: Should be close; variance arises from sequence length distribution and KV cache warmup. We always recommend running a replay using your traffic pattern — our Optimize modal can generate suggested batching and KV cache heuristics. We'll run a seed replay for LumenHealth. 04:06 Jordan: Quick sidebar — routing with prefix cache can reduce p50 by up to 30% on repeat prompts; for clinical summarization you may have lots of repeated sentence starts so caching helps. 04:16 Alex: Interesting. Could you show how Optimize suggests batching? 04:18 Priya: Sure. Opening Optimize -> Bench harness. You upload a sample of requests and it shows recommended batch sizes per hardware, plus expected throughput and per-token cost under different quantization profiles. Here we have a simulated run: for open-clarity-7B-v2 on A10G q8 gives 180ms p50 with batch size=8; q4 drops latency but also model quality in some cases. 04:42 Samir: I'm trying to parse the compatibility matrix — I see some models incompatible with certain kernels; what does that mean in practice? 04:49 Mateo: The matrix maps model ops to tested kernels, and flags possible operator fallbacks. If a kernel isn't available on your hardware we may run a slower fallback kernel which increases latency. The console also flags when a model requires a new CUDA kernel or special lib. 05:02 Rina: Do you maintain per-model notes about known hallucination patterns or prompts that trip up specific models? 05:07 Priya: Yes, the curation notes include failure modes, prompt templates to avoid, and example eval prompts. You can also attach your own eval set to watch quality regressions — Redwood will raise alerts if a new model variant regresses on your golden prompts. 05:20 Jules: On pricing: if we run Dedicated vs Hosted is cost per token different? 05:25 Jordan: Hosted is fully managed pricing; Dedicated gives you predictable throughput (reserved) and slightly lower token price depending on commit. Private on-prem is licensed differently — usually platform fee + infra. We'll share an estimate. 05:38 Alex: Competitors we've looked at (Anthropic endpoints, Self-hosted Triton infra) — how do you compare on ease of onboarding? 05:47 Jordan: Redwood provides a single API and console, plus migration guides and a sample helm chart for Private. Our focused differentiator is the runtime-level optimizations (kernel selection, prefix caching, routing) built-in so you don't have to tune everything. 05:59 Priya: Back to the demo: I want to show the 'comparison view' — select two models, run a synthetic benchmark across your sample traffic. The UI displays delta in ROUGE, p50/p95, tokens charged, and a cost-normalized quality metric. You can set threshold rules like 'select model if cost-normalized quality > 0.85'. 06:20 Rina: Can we automate selection per route? For example, pick medlite for transcript summarization where accuracy matters, open-clarity for triage notes where speed matters. 06:29 Priya: Absolutely — per-route model assignment is first-class. You can also attach routing rules: region, customer tier, pinned model, fallback chain. 06:36 Mateo: Also mention cold start behavior — KV cache cold starts can add overhead. We advise a small keep-warm traffic or pre-warming policy for critical routes. 06:47 Samir: Encryption concerns — when using Redwood Private with our KMS, where do keys live? 06:52 Jordan: Keys remain in your KMS/HSM; Redwood's control plane talks to the KMS but logs only store a key reference. We'll include the HSM integration doc and SOC2 artifact. 06:59 Alex: Ok, practical step: which two models should we pilot with? 07:02 Priya: My recommended pair: open-clarity-7B-v2 (low-cost, fast) + medlite-13B-q4 (higher quality, A100-optimized). We'll baseline both with your sample of 5k notes and run a replay on Dedicated test pool. 07:15 Rina: Timeline? We can scope a two-week pilot. 07:19 Jordan: Sounds good. We'll provision a small Dedicated pool for the replay and run both models in parallel. 07:24 Jules: What do you need from us to start? 07:27 Jordan: 1) sample dataset (5k anonymized notes), 2) target evaluation metrics (we'll use ROUGE + domain-specific checks), 3) a security contact for Private docs. 07:36 Samir: I can be that contact. 07:38 Jordan: Great. We'll also need an estimated throughput target so we size the Dedicated pool; a small 4-GPU pool should be fine for the replay. 07:46 Alex: One more — how do rollbacks work if a new model is worse in production? 07:50 Priya: Automatic rollback policies: you can set a regression threshold and on detection traffic flows back to the previous pinned model and an incident is opened. 07:58 Jordan: Ok let's capture next steps. 08:01 Jordan: Summarizing: Redwood to share pilot quote, security pack, and a benchmarking spreadsheet template. LumenHealth to share sample notes and define evaluation metric. Schedule the pilot kickoff next week. 08:15 Jules: Quick note — the bench sheet link in chat has some preliminary latency numbers and a column showing 'kernel hint' which was helpful. 08:23 Priya: We'll also add recommended prompt templates and a short script to run the replay harness. 08:28 Jordan: Any final questions? 08:30 Samir: No, we covered it. 08:32 Alex: Thanks, this was helpful. 08:34 Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up via email with links and the quote. 08:38 [meeting ends]

Redwood: Upload bench spreadsheet template and replay script link by 2026-05-13
LumenHealth: Provide 5k anonymized clinical notes and evaluation criteria by 2026-05-15
Samir (LumenHealth): Confirm security contact and supply SOC2 scope details by 2026-05-14

Run replay with open-clarity-7B-v2 and medlite-13B-q4 on Dedicated test pool
